Article Title: 'INS Mahendragiri symbol of Atmanirbhar Bharat': PM Modi in Mann Ki Baat
Article Text:
PM Modi addressed 136th episode of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday highlighted India's growing self-reliance in the defence sector, saying the country is continuously strengthening its technological capabilities alongside the courage of its armed forces.Addressing the 136th episode of his monthly radio programme, Mann Ki Baat, the Prime Minister pointed to the induction of INS Mahendragiri into the Indian Navy as an example of India's progress in indigenous defence manufacturing."This modern warship has been designed in India and made in India. More than 75 per cent indigenous content has been used in this. This is a symbol of the growing strength of ' Atmanirbhar Bharat '," he said.PM Modi also referred to the indigenously developed Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket (LRGR-120), an advanced precision-guided artillery rocket system developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation.The system has a validated strike range of 60 km to 120 km."Behind this success, it is the collective hardwork of our scientists and engineers," he said.The Prime Minister also highlighted the successful flight test of the Khusha Missile, describing it as another milestone in India's expanding indigenous defence capabilities.Later in his address, PM Modi paid homage to the soldiers who fought in the 1999 Kargil War , saying Kargil Vijay Diwas fills every Indian with pride and serves as a reminder of the extraordinary courage displayed by the armed forces."There are certain dates in our lives for which we do not need to look at the calendar. Today, July 26, is one such date. Today is the Kargil Vijay Diwas. This day fills us with pride and reminds us of the extraordinary courage of our brave soldiers," he said."The towering peaks of Kargil, harsh weather, the challenges posed by the enemy, our soldiers faced every such circumstance, yet their morale was greater than any challenge. They sacrificed everything for protecting the motherland. Today, on Kargil Vijay Diwas, I pay homage to all the brave martyrs and soldiers," he added.PM Modi said today's India not only remembers the sacrifices of its bravehearts but also ensures that their stories reach younger generations.Referring to this year's commemorative events, he said a special Shaurya Vijay Yatra was organised to honour the legacy of the Kargil War. The motorcycle expedition began on July 14 from the National War Memorial in New Delhi and will culminate at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras."Its message is 'One ride, one nation, one salute'. This expedition reminds us that the sacrifices made for the country can never be forgotten," the Prime Minister said.Recalling his appeal from the previous edition of the programme, the Prime Minister said the campaign has gathered momentum across the country, with people from villages and cities actively contributing to water conservation initiatives."In the previous episode of 'Mann Ki Baat', I spoke to you about the 'Catch The Rain' campaign. I had appealed that this campaign to conserve every drop of rain be turned into a mass movement. The message of 'Catch The Rain' is very simple: conserve the water right where and when the rain falls. That is why a special nationwide campaign has been underway since July 4. Under this initiative, fresh momentum is being given to rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, the rejuvenation of old water bodies, and tree plantation," PM Modi said.He expressed satisfaction over the enthusiastic response received from citizens, local bodies and community organisations, saying the campaign has witnessed widespread participation across different parts of the country."I am delighted to see overwhelming participation from people everywhere -- be it villages or cities, panchayats or social organisations. At some places, silt is being removed from old ponds, while at others, wells and stepwells are being revived. Borewells no longer in use are now serving as channels for groundwater recharge," he added.Highlighting examples from several states, the Prime Minister said large-scale water conservation work has already produced encouraging results.He noted that nearly 1,500 ponds have been built in Madhya Pradesh's Sidhi district, 'Amrit Sarovars' have been restored in Narsinghpur, and Maharashtra's Nashik has significantly enhanced its water storage capacity through the campaign.He also pointed to Andhra Pradesh's Nandyal district, where every gram panchayat joined the initiative and old ponds were revived to restore their utility."Our cities as well are not lagging behind either; encouraging results from this campaign are visible in Korba (Chhattisgarh), Bhubaneswar (Odisha), and Vizianagaram (Andhra Pradesh)," PM Modi said.Urging people to continue contributing to water conservation efforts, the Prime Minister appealed to citizens to take responsibility for preserving water bodies in their neighbourhoods, stressing that every drop of water saved today would benefit future generations."Come, let us also take responsibility for a pond, well, or stepwell in our vicinity -- save every drop of water. Every drop saved today serves as the greatest asset for the future of coming generations," he added.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted India's growing self-reliance in the defence sector. He said the country is continuously strengthening its technological capabilities alongside the courage of its armed forces. PM Modi paid homage to the soldiers who fought in the 1999 Kargil War.

Article Title: 'Every misadventure by Pakistan will draw response beyond their imagination': Rajnath Singh on Vijay Diwas
Article Text:
'Indebted to all those valiant soldiers'

'Army fully prepared'

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday issued a stern warning to Pakistan, saying every "misadventure" would invite a response "beyond their imagination".While addressing the nation on the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas at the Kargil War Memorial in Drass, Ladakh, he said, ""Our intention is clear. There will be no talks with Pakistan. If there are any talks, they will be only on PoK, which is a part of India and illegally occupied by Pakistan. ""At present, Pakistan has made terrorism a part of its government policy, and the distinction between the military and militants has completely disappeared there. The army not only protects terrorist organizations but also works closely with them. Therefore, during Operation Sindoor, we made it clear that India will no longer view terrorists and the governments that support them separately," he added.Drawing a sharp contrast between India and Pakistan, Defence minister Rajnath Singh further said that India is focused on innovation, technology and development, while Pakistan continues to promote infiltration and terrorism."India is pursuing innovation, while Pakistan is seeking new ways of infiltration. While India is designing ships, Pakistan is engaged in designing terrorism," he said.In his address while reiterating India's firm stand on Pakistan, Rajnath Singh said there would be no talks with Islamabad, except on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), which he described as an integral part of India under illegal occupation."Our intention is clear. There will be no talks with Pakistan. If there are any talks, they will be only on PoK, which is a part of India and illegally occupied by Pakistan."In an X post on Sunday, Singh wrote, "On the occasion of Kargil Vijay Diwas, I pay my deepest respects to all the brave soldiers who laid down their lives in the defense of our motherland. The nation will forever remain grateful and indebted to all those valiant soldiers who demonstrated extraordinary valor on the inaccessible peaks of Kargil in 1999."He added that the Indian Army 's indomitable courage, sacrifice and unwavering resolve would continue to inspire future generations with patriotism, dedication to duty and "the spirit of offering everything for the motherland."Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday asserted that the Indian Army is "fully prepared" to tackle any challenge, saying the "intent of infiltrators" has remained unchanged since the 1999 Kargil conflict.Speaking to Army personnel at a Shaurya Bhoj in Dras on Kargil Vijay Diwas, after attending Shaurya Sandhya at the Kargil War Memorial, Singh paid tribute to the soldiers who laid down their lives during the 1999 war and said that while India celebrates their sacrifice, the country must remain vigilant against continuing threats such as proxy war and cross-border infiltration."We have to remember that even today challenges have not reduced; the intent of infiltrators hasn't changed, and even today it adopts tools like a proxy war or infiltration," Singh said, in an apparent reference to Pakistan."I am fully assured that our Army is fully prepared for any such challenges," he added.Observed every year on July 26, Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorates India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War, honours the 527 soldiers who laid down their lives during Operation Vijay and pays tribute to the courage of thousands who fought in one of the world's toughest battlefields.
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday issued a stern warning to Pakistan. He said every "misadventure" would invite a response "beyond their imagination" Singh said there would be no talks with Islamabad, except on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK)

Article Title: Nepal eases rules on Indian currency, allows Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes up to Rs 25,000
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Nepal has eased restrictions on the movement of Indian currency, allowing Indian and Nepali citizens to carry Indian Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes issued after November 9, 2016. According to the Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), the permitted notes can be carried into or taken out of Nepal up to a limit of Rs 25,000 per person.According to news agency PTI, the revised rules permit citizens of both countries to bring the approved currency notes into Nepal, carry them within the country, or take them out, subject to existing regulations.In its latest notice, the NRB clarified that older Indian currency notes issued before the 2016 demonetisation period will continue to remain prohibited in Nepal.The NRB added that only redesigned Indian Rs 500 notes and Rs 200 notes introduced after November 9, 2016, will be permitted under the new arrangement.The central bank had initially published the provision in the Nepal Gazette on February 11. However, it issued another notice on Thursday to clarify the implementation process and address concerns over cross-border currency movement.NRB spokesperson Guru Prasad Paudel said Nepali citizens would not be allowed to bring Indian currency into Nepal from countries other than India.He also clarified that Indian currency taken out of Nepal by Nepali citizens could only be carried to India and not to any third country.The new provision would facilitate Indian tourists visiting Nepal and Nepalese nationals engaged in trade and business with India, said Paudel.The rule change comes after years of restrictions introduced following India’s demonetisation announcement on November 8, 2016, when the old Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes were withdrawn from circulation.Following the move, Nepal had restricted the use and movement of those discontinued Indian notes due to concerns over their circulation and financial impact.The latest decision affects cross-border transactions between India and Nepal, which share an open border and extensive economic links. India remains Nepal’s largest trading partner and a key source of tourists, while thousands of Nepali citizens travel to India for work, education and business.The NRB also stated that Nepali citizens and foreign visitors can bring foreign currency worth up to $5,000, or its equivalent in other currencies, into Nepal without filing a customs declaration. Amounts above that threshold must be declared upon arrival.
Article Summary: Nepal has eased restrictions on the movement of Indian currency. Indian and Nepali citizens can carry Indian Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes issued after November 9, 2016. The permitted notes can be carried into or taken out of Nepal up to a limit of Rs 25,000.

Article Title: 'Gratitude to brave soldiers': PM Modi pays tribute to Kargil heroes on 27th Vijay Diwas
Article Text:
India is observing the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday paid tribute to the soldiers of the Indian Armed Forces on the occasion of the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas and remembered their role in safeguarding the country's sovereignty."On Kargil Vijay Diwas, our nation expresses gratitude to the brave soldiers for their extraordinary courage and commitment towards securing India. Their valour in the face of the most formidable conditions will forever remain a source of national pride. Their unwavering patriotism and devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations," the Prime Minister said in a post on X.India is observing the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas, commemorating its victory in the 1999 Kargil War. The day marks the successful culmination of Operation Vijay and honours the 527 soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while driving Pakistani intruders out of strategic heights in the Kargil sector.The Kargil conflict, fought between May and July 1999, remains the only conventional war between two nuclear-armed neighbours. The battles were fought across the rugged mountain terrain of Kargil, Dras, Batalik, Mushkoh and Kaksar in Ladakh at altitudes exceeding 5,000 metres.Despite freezing temperatures, low oxygen levels and heavily fortified enemy positions, Indian troops recaptured the occupied peaks without crossing the Line of Control, earning global recognition for their professionalism and military restraint.Over the years, Kargil Vijay Diwas has come to symbolise not only India's military victory but also a defining moment that reshaped the country's defence preparedness, strategic planning and national security framework.Union home minister Amit Shah also paid tribute to the soldiers, describing Kargil Vijay Diwas as a symbol of the Indian Army's indomitable courage and extraordinary valour."'Kargil Vijay Diwas' stands as a symbol of the Indian Army's indomitable courage and extraordinary valour. In 1999, despite facing adverse conditions and enemy positions situated at high altitudes amidst the treacherous, snow-capped peaks of the Himalayas, our brave soldiers forced the enemy to their knees through 'Operation Vijay'. On 'Kargil Vijay Diwas', I pay tribute to all those brave sons who made the ultimate sacrifice to uphold the nation's integrity," Shah said.Defence minister Rajnath Singh , who attended the Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorations at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras on Saturday, said the intent of infiltrators had not changed since the 1999 conflict and asserted that the Indian Army remained fully prepared to counter any challenge."We have to remember that even today challenges have not reduced; the intent of infiltrators hasn't changed, and even today it adopts tools like a proxy war or infiltration," Singh said in an apparent reference to Pakistan."I am fully assured that our Army is fully prepared for any such challenges," he added.The defence minister also highlighted the government's focus on modernising the armed forces, saying sustained efforts were being made to equip the military with the latest technology and the best training. Referring to the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, he expressed confidence that the Indian armed forces would emerge among the finest in the world.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also remembered the fallen soldiers, saying the nation would forever remain indebted to their courage, valour and supreme sacrifice."A humble tribute to all the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while defending India's borders, on Kargil Victory Day. The nation will forever remain indebted to your courage, valor, and supreme sacrifice," Gandhi wrote on X.
Article Summary: India is observing the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas. The day marks the successful culmination of Operation Vijay. 527 soldiers made the supreme sacrifice while driving Pakistani intruders out of strategic heights in the Kargill sector.

Article Title: ICMR hands over homegrown cervical pre-cancer treatment, vaccine technologies to pharma firms
Article Text:
ICMR transfers medical technologies under Patent Mitra Initiative

NEW DELHI: A potential new treatment for cervical pre-cancer and two next-generation vaccines against typhoid and other gut infections have moved a step closer to becoming available in India after the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) licensed the technologies to Indian pharmaceutical companies. If successful, the indigenous products could improve access to affordable treatment and vaccines while reducing dependence on imported technologies.The technologies have been transferred under ICMR’s Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative, which helps convert government-funded research into products that can be developed, tested and eventually brought to the market.Among them is SHetA2, a potential treatment for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN), a precancerous condition caused by persistent infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV). If left untreated, CIN can progress to cervical cancer, one of the leading cancers among Indian women.Unlike surgery, which is commonly used to remove abnormal cells, SHetA2 is designed to selectively destroy HPV-infected abnormal cells while sparing healthy cells. Scientists believe it could offer women a safer and less invasive treatment option in the future. The technology has been licensed to Emcure Pharmaceuticals for further development, clinical testing and commercialisation.ICMR has also licensed two vaccine technologies developed by its National Institute for Research in Bacterial Infections (NIRBI), Kolkata, to Biological E. One is a next-generation vaccine against typhoid, while the other is designed to protect against typhoid, paratyphoid and Shigella, bacteria that cause severe diarrhoea and other intestinal infections, particularly among children.The vaccine candidates will now undergo further development and evaluation before they can be considered for regulatory approval and public use.Dr Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research, and Director General, ICMR, said partnerships between researchers and industry are helping move promising discoveries from laboratories to patients while strengthening India’s biomedical innovation ecosystem.The technology transfer is part of ICMR’s broader effort to support indigenous healthcare innovation through patent protection, technology licensing, clinical validation and regulatory facilitation, with the aim of making affordable medicines and vaccines available to patients.
Article Summary: The technologies have been transferred under ICMR’s Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative. If successful, the indigenous products could improve access to affordable treatment and vaccines while reducing dependence on imported technologies. Among them is a potential treatment for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN)

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns: Government took exit call after Wangchuk breakthrough failed to end protests
Article Text:
Govt took exit call after Wangchuk breakthrough failed to end protests

NEW DELHI: BJP has fended off numerous opposition campaigns built around allegations, contentious laws or policies, and suspected wrongdoings of a senior Union minister or a chief minister since PM Modi took office in 2014 without making any appearance of bowing to pressure. However, where the opposition could not succeed, street protests and the fear that they could have triggered violence have.The resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, a key member of the Cabinet since Modi first took office in 2014, following unebbing protests is a significant political dent to the party, presenting the opposition a rare opening to build on youth anger after suffering electoral setbacks and desertions from ranks.Govt hoped to benefit from the optics of activist Sonam Wangchuk breaking his 26-day hunger strike by accepting soup from Union minister J P Nadda and agreeing to the gentle terms built on assurances.With the protests, though, showing no signs of a let-up and Rahul Gandhi stepping up opposition's stir, BJP chose pragmatism over defiance, more so as it was confronted with Gen Z that did not deal in the old grammar of politics, making its irreverent slogans, memes and skits go viral.Earlier, government had withdrawn farm laws in Nov 2021 following a year-long protest from farmers, while Modi had publicly announced in Dec 2019 that his govt had no plans for a National Register of Citizens to defuse the agitation against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act.J Akbar, who quit in 2018 after his name surfaced in the #MeToo row, was a junior minister and carried little political heft. As BJP counts its losses, it will have to grapple with the challenge of winning over a generation which, many political observers say, had been showing signs of restiveness over a host of employment-related concerns even before these protests broke out, despite a section supporting the party’s other planks. The view within BJP is that despite the immediate political price it has paid, it has shown its sincerity of purpose by engaging with protesters and conceding to them, belying the charge that it was “arrogant and insensitive
Article Summary: Govt hoped to benefit from the optics of activist Sonam Wangchuk breaking his 26-day hunger strike by accepting soup from Union minister J P Nadda. With protests showing no signs of a let-up and Rahul Gandhi stepping up opposition's stir, BJP chose pragmatism over defiance.

Article Title: Pralhad Joshi, man with a low profile & an effective style
Article Text:
Pralhad Joshi named new education minister

NEW DELHI: Pralhad Venkatesh Joshi, the new Union education minister, is one of BJP's most experienced parliamentarians and has been in PM Narendra Modi's Cabinet since 2019. The five-time MP from Karnataka also served as president of BJP's Karnataka unit and played a key role in expanding party's footprint in the state before coming to the Centre.Known for his low-profile yet effective style, Joshi has handled important parliamentary and ministerial responsibilities over the years. Before his latest assignment as education minister, he was in charge of consumer affairs, food and public distribution, and new and renewable energy ministries, portfolios that will stay with him.In 2019, he was sworn-in as cabinet minister and given charge of the portfolios of parliamentary affairs, coal and mines until 2024. As parliamentary affairs minister, he handled the passage of key legislation, including the abrogation of Article 370 and the Women's Reservation Bill."Under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, I will work to the best of my ability and fulfil my responsibilities with dedication," Joshi told reporters.
Article Summary: Pralhad Joshi is one of BJP's most experienced parliamentarians. He has been in PM Narendra Modi's Cabinet since 2019. Joshi was in charge of consumer affairs, food and public distribution, and new and renewable energy ministries, portfolios that will stay with him.

Article Title: 'Country, youth & students far more important than any post': Amit Shah on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister
Article Text:
Amit Shah reacted to Pradhan's exit, says 'government respects sentiments of country's youth'

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, saying the BJP considers the country, youth and students more important than any position while reaffirming the Modi government's commitment to reforms against paper leaks.In a post on X, Shah said, "For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji from his post exemplifies this very principle."Shah further added that the government respected the sentiments of students and remained committed to introducing reforms to prevent paper leaks, while expressing confidence that those responsible would be punished and justice would be ensured for NEET aspirants."The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable. I am fully confident that these steps will ensure complete justice for the students who succeeded in the NEET examination."He further highlighted Pradhan's tenure as education minister, crediting him with advancing several key education initiatives, including the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), expansion of examinations in mother tongues, PM SHRI Schools, digital education, skill development and industry-academia collaboration."During his tenure, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has brought about significant reforms in the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), arrangements for examinations in mother tongues, expansion of PM SHRI Schools, promotion of digital education, skill development, and strengthening industry-academia coordination. His efforts toward making the examination system more inclusive and student-centric have also been noteworthy. His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation."Read more: Dharmendra Pradhan out, Pralhad Joshi in; CJP exits Jantar Mantar, exam reform Bill to enter LS - key points Earlier on Saturday, Shah had also visited Pradhan's residence along with finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman and commerce and industries minister Piyush Goyal, as mark of solidarity.Pradhan resigned as Union education minister earlier on Saturday, amid nationwide protests over NEET-UG paper leak controversy. Hours later, senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the education ministry, while the Centre reached an agreement with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), leading to the withdrawal of its protest after 36 days at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Amit Shah says 'government respects sentiments of country's youth' Reiterates commitment to reforms against paper leaks. Praises Dharmendra Pradhan's tenure as education minister, crediting him with advancing key education initiatives. Pralhad Joshi has been given additional charge of the education ministry.

Article Title: Amit Shah & other top BJP functionaries call on Pradhan at his residence to show solidarity
Article Text:
BJP figures, including home minister Amit Shah, visited Dharmendra Pradhan’s residence in a show of solidarity after he resigned

NEW DELHI: A steady stream of leading BJP figures, including home minister Amit Shah , visited Dharmendra Pradhan 's residence in a show of solidarity after he resigned as education minister owing to student protests over the NEET paper leak.Besides Shah, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman and commerce and industries minister Piyush Goyal were among the key Union Cabinet members who met Pradhan, who has handled crucial political assignments, including state elections.Shah said Pradhan helmed "bold reforms" by implementing NEP, placing emphasis on mother tongues, and making exams more inclusive and student-centric. He added, however, that the country and the young generation were more important to BJP than any office, saying, "Modi govt respects the youth's sentiments and is committed to necessary reforms against paper leaks."Party president Nitin Nabin said BJP "stood firmly" with Pradhan."He played a pivotal role in reforming India's education landscape and successfully implementing the landmark NEP... Prioritising larger interests, his decision to step down reflects the highest standards of integrity and selfless service in public life," Nabin added.The tributes are a firm indication that Pradhan remains a valuable figure for BJP despite his exit owing to political necessities.Defence minister Rajnath Singh said Pradhan's tenure reflected his commitment to transforming India into a developed nation. "His contribution to public service has been inclusive, foresighted, and aligned with the aspirations of a new India," he added.Another ministerial colleague, Kiren Rijiju, praised Pradhan for his dedication to strengthening India's education ecosystem. "Leading such a critical sector demands immense persever-ance, and he embraced it with courage and clear vision," he said.
Article Summary: A steady stream of leading BJP figures, including home minister Amit Shah, visited Dharmendra Pradhan’s residence in a show of solidarity after he resigned as education minister. The tributes are a firm indication thatPradhan remains a valuable figure for BJP despite his exit owing to political necessities.

Article Title: Pralhad Joshi named new education minister after Prez Murmu accepts Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Pralhad Joshi named new education minister after Prez Murmu accepts Pradhan's resignation

NEW DELHI: BJP leader Pralhad Joshi on Saturday was appointed as the new Union education minister, hours after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.Pradhan resigned taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that triggered weeks of nationwide student protests. His resignation was accepted by President Droupadi Murmu.A press release by Rashtrapati Bhavan read: "The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio.After being appointed as education minister Pralhad Joshi said he accepted the additional charge of the education ministry with 'a sense of duty and humility' and pledged to work under the guidance of PM Modi to further strengthen the country's education system."I accept this responsibility with a sense of duty and humility. I am thankful to the Prime Minister. In the last 12 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, many historic achievements have been made.In the last four to five years, Dharmendra Pradhan also implemented the National Education Policy, and several important initiatives were undertaken. The country has made significant progress in the new education system. Under the guidance of the Prime Minister, I will work to the best of my ability and fulfil my responsibilities with dedication," Joshi said.Joshi, the Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad constituency also hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. A five-time MP, he has previously served as the Union minister for coal, mines and parliamentary affairs.As the minister for new and renewable energy, Joshi has been leading the Centre's efforts to expand clean energy capacity, with a focus on achieving 500 GW of renewable and non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2070.He has overseen key initiatives including the National Green Hydrogen Mission, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM scheme and offshore wind energy projects, while pushing for annual bids for 50 GW of renewable energy capacity and other policy measures to boost the sector.His appointment comes at a crucial time as the education ministry implements sweeping reforms following the NEET -UG controversy, including the restructuring of the National Testing Agency (NTA), stricter anti-paper leak measures and a shift to computer-based testing for NEET from 2027.
Article Summary: Pralhad Joshi named new education minister after Prez Murmu accepts Pradhan's resignation. Joshi said he accepted the additional charge of the education ministry with 'a sense of duty and humility' He pledged to work under the guidance of PM Modi to further strengthen the country's education system.

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan out, Pralhad Joshi in: CJP exits Jantar Mantar, exam reform Bill to enter LS - key points
Article Text:
CJP protestors and students celebrate after Pradhan's resignation

Here are the top developments:

Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education ministry

Metro stations reopen after protest ends

Pradhan resigns, cites moral responsibility

Centre and CJP reach agreement after third round of talks

Student movement ends after 36 days

Opposition calls it a victory for students

Wangchuk welcomes outcome

Tougher anti-paper leak law proposed

Biggest political fallout of NEET controversy

NEW DELHI: Saturday witnessed a series of major developments in the NEET paper leak controversy, beginning with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation after weeks of nationwide protests.Hours later, Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new education minister getting additional charge apart from portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution.Meanwhile, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) held a third round of talks, after which the government agreed to withdraw FIRs filed against peaceful protesters.Following the meeting, the CJP announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar, saying it was ending the protest in "good faith" after the government accepted its key demands.The protest site was cleared after the CJP demands were met.The developments marked the biggest political fallout of the NEET controversy, which triggered nationwide student protests, a CBI probe and sweeping reforms to India's examination system.Hours after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, President Droupadi Murmu assigned senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi the additional charge of the Union education ministry on the advice of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.A five-time Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad, Joshi will continue to hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. He takes charge at a crucial time as the government rolls out reforms following the NEET-UG paper leak, including restructuring the NTA, tightening exam security and shifting NEET to computer-based testing from 2027.After being given the charge, Joshi said: "The Prime Minister has placed his trust in me and has entrusted me with such a significant responsibility. With complete humility and a strong sense of responsibility, I will fulfil this duty...I thank the Prime Minister for giving me this important responsibility and for showing such great confidence in me. Under his guidance and leadership, I will work sincerely and try my best to meet his expectations in this department. With full dedication, humility, and honesty, I will work towards fulfilling this responsibility. I once again thank the Prime Minister for giving me this opportunity."Normal Metro access resumed across Delhi after the CJP called off its 36-day protest, with the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) reopening the entry gates of all stations that had been closed because of security arrangements.The reopening came shortly after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre reached an agreement with the CJP to end the agitation.Earlier in the day, the DMRC had resumed services at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat stations before restoring entry and exit at all 18 affected stations, which had been placed under restrictions due to the protests near Jantar Mantar.Announcing his resignation in a letter addressed to the country's youth, Pradhan said he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country.He said he had spent more than four decades working for students, teachers and education reforms and had always believed that a strong education system was the foundation of a strong nation. Pradhan said the government acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination by handing the investigation to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a fresh test, while also deciding to shift NEET to computer-based mode from next year.He added that he had accepted responsibility from the very beginning and had worked to ensure that no deserving student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia.Recalling the events of the past few days had deeply saddened him, Pradhan said he was stepping down to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation, safeguard national unity and allow students to focus on their education.Hours after Pradhan's resignation, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party held a third round of talks, following which the student group announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day protest.Addressing a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das said the agitation was being withdrawn in good faith after the government accepted its key demands.The CJP said its primary demand, Pradhan's resignation, had been fulfilled. It also said the Centre had agreed to withdraw FIRs and legal cases against peaceful protesters and assured that no retaliatory action would be taken.The government further agreed to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide in accordance with existing rules and regulations and promised to consider the CJP's five-point charter on examination reforms.JP Nadda said the government had sympathetically considered the delegation's demands and would hold further discussions on long-term reforms to strengthen the examination system.The CJP protest began at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding accountability over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak, wider reforms in the examination system and Pradhan's resignation.The movement gained national attention after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the agitation with an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health and later hospitalisation intensified public attention and increased pressure on the government.Although Wangchuk ended his 26-day fast after receiving written assurances from the Centre, the CJP continued its protest until Pradhan resigned and the remaining demands were addressed.Speaking after the agreement, Ashutosh Ranka appealed to protesters across the country to withdraw peacefully, while Saurav Das said the movement was ending with the understanding that all commitments would be implemented within the agreed timelines."Government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protest; we urge everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites," CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said.Earlier in the day, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had briefly said the protest would continue until all demands were accepted. After the talks concluded, however, the organisation announced the end of the agitation.Dipke also urged supporters not to treat Pradhan's resignation as a personal victory for him, saying the movement was driven by thousands of young people and should remain focused on institutional reforms rather than individuals.Amit Shah reacts to Pradhan's exitUnion home minister Amit Shah reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's exit as education minister saying, "Modi government respects youth's sentiments"."For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan ji from his post exemplifies this very principle. The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable. I am fully confident that these steps will ensure complete justice for the students who succeeded in the NEET examination.," he said."During his tenure, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has brought about significant reforms in the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), arrangements for examinations in mother tongues, expansion of PM SHRI Schools, promotion of digital education, skill development, and strengthening industry-academia coordination. His efforts toward making the examination system more inclusive and student-centric have also been noteworthy. His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation," he added.The opposition described Pradhan's resignation as a major victory for students and renewed calls for broader reforms in the education system.Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called the resignation "the victory of the future of India", saying Pradhan had become a symbol of corruption, incompetence and the decline of the country's education system.He said the government must now introduce meaningful reforms and alleged that the issue of police action against student protesters would remain a key matter during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge termed the resignation a "victory of truth" and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to the country's youth while ensuring action against those responsible for the alleged use of force against protesters.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal described the development as a "big win for democracy", while Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar said the Congress would continue raising issues concerning students and maintained that peaceful protests were an essential part of democracy.Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk welcomed the developments, describing them as "a victory of democracy, direct democracy, peace, patience and perseverance". He congratulated the student movement and thanked citizens across the country for supporting the agitation.His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, also praised the role played by India's younger generation, saying the protests had demonstrated courage, patriotism and commitment to democratic values without violence.The Centre has proposed major amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure faster investigations, time-bound trials and stricter punishment for paper leaks and examination malpractice.The proposed Bill provides for the creation of Special Task Forces (STFs) to investigate offences, completion of investigations within two months, day-to-day hearings in special fast-track courts and disposal of appeals by High Courts within three months.It also significantly increases penalties, proposing jail terms of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 10 crore for organised paper leak rackets, along with tougher action against service providers and officials found involved in examination fraud.Pradhan's resignation marks the most significant political consequence of the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, which began after allegations of question paper leaks in the May 3 examination.The controversy led to the cancellation of the examination, a nationwide CBI investigation, repeated protests, parliamentary disruptions, changes to the anti-paper leak law and a major restructuring of the National Testing Agency.Pradhan also removed education minister from his X bio following the resignation.
Article Summary: Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education ministry. Delhi Metro stations reopen after protest ends. Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns, cites moral responsibility. Centre and Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP) reach agreement after third round of talks.

Article Title: Ram Temple donation theft row: UP govt reconstitutes SIT; IG Kiran S to lead probe
Article Text:
UP govt reconstitutes SIT probing Ram Temple donation theft row after SC orders

NEW DELHI: Acting on the Supreme Court's directions, the Uttar Pradesh government has constituted a new Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by senior IPS officers to investigate the alleged embezzlement of devotees' offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.The reconstituted team is headed by Inspector General Kiran S, with Deputy Inspector General Somen Verma and Ayodhya Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Gaurav Grover as members. It replaces the earlier SIT, which was headed by Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and included Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar among its members.The apex court had, during a July 13 hearing, expressed the view that allegations involving theft and financial irregularities required investigation by experienced police officers.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohan directed the state to form a fresh SIT under a senior IPS officer and submit a status report by July 27.The case centres on allegations that offerings made by devotees at the Ram temple were siphoned off instead of being deposited through the prescribed process.Investigators probing the case earlier examined CCTV footage, donation registers, cash-handling records and financial documents, besides questioning temple staff.Their preliminary findings indicated suspected irregularities in the counting and deposit of donations.The investigation led to the arrest of several accused, while police seized cash, vehicles, investment documents and other assets allegedly acquired using the misappropriated funds. Investigators also analysed bank transactions and other digital evidence to trace the alleged money trail.With the new SIT now taking over the probe, the Uttar Pradesh government is expected to place its findings before the Supreme Court in a status report on July 27.
Article Summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has constituted a new Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by senior IPS officers. The SIT will investigate the alleged embezzlement of devotees' offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya. The reconstituted team is headed by Inspector General Kiran S.

Article Title: Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric national identity card as travel document
Article Text:
Nepal seeks India's approval for biometric National Identity card as travel document (ANI image)

Nepal plans to replace citizenship certificates

India reviews the proposal

The Kathmandu Post

Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document for cross-border journeys, alongside passports and citizenship certificates.At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or an original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.However, Nepal's National Identity card contains biometric information, including fingerprints, facial images and iris scans. The programme was launched as a pilot in Panchthar district and among government employees in 2009.So far, more than 4.5 million Nepali citizens have received the card, while nearly 20 million applications have been submitted.The request comes as Nepal gradually makes the biometric National Identity card mandatory for banking, land registration, passport issuance and access to public services, with plans to eventually replace citizenship certificates."In the long run, we will have a single identity card replacing the citizenship certificate.It is verified, authentic and technology-friendly," Tiwari said."That is why we have requested India to allow the use of the National Identity Card while travelling by both air and land routes," he added.According to senior immigration officials quoted by, an Indian Embassy delegation met officials from Nepal's Department of Immigration earlier this week to discuss the proposalThe delegation was reportedly "positive" about the initiative and informed Nepalese officials that the request had been forwarded to authorities in New Delhi for consideration."We have already forwarded the proposal to the Indian side through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," said Ram Chandra Tiwari, Director General of the Department of Immigration.Officials from Nepal's Home Ministry also said that discussions have included creating formal mechanisms to record cross-border travel data and better manage movement between the two neighbouring countries.
Article Summary: Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document. At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.

Article Title: Left scores win, despite its shrunken presence, through its student organs
Article Text:
When the Left-aligned student groups joined the CJP-led protest, they were drawn into the fold organically, said parties’ functionaries

NEW DELHI: It must qualify as a striking case of maximising one's returns on meagre capital. Disproportionate to its marginal presence in Parliament and anaemic strength on the ground, Left parties successfully leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which have active units in Delhi, to pressure govt to give into the demand of getting Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as education minister.In fact, AISA members, president Neha Bora and Manish Kumar and Ameen Amitoj, despite having no prior association with Abhijeet Dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students.The victory of their student outfits, which made common cause with those sections of Gen Z, who are usually not receptive to their "class warfare" trope, could act as a compensation of sorts for the Left in an electorally bleak season, marked by routs in Kerala and West Bengal.Earlier, in another instance of them successfully using their tactical intelligence, the Left, through its farmers' wings, influenced the protests in Punjab against farm sector reforms laws enacted by Modi govt, which had to junk them.If AISA, SFI and AISF were a vocal presence throughout the protest, their mother outfits CPI(ML), CPM and CPI, in that order, complemented the effort on the ground by goading the opposition to support the CJP-led protests.According to Left functionaries, who have been part of the demonstrations, when the Left-aligned students groups joined the students' protest led by CJP, they were drawn into the fold organically and not perceived as people just jumping in for credit as these students have been raising issues around the flaws in the examination system and the challenges through their unions.All 15 MPs belonging to the Left joined the students to protest the police action against them during the march to Parliament on July 20. They also ensured there was no dilution of the demand for Pradhan's resignation.CPI(ML) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya agreed that the success of the protests has given the Left a fillip. "This movement has re-energised ongoing struggles across the country for democracy, justice, and the defence of the Constitution." He called upon INDIA bloc to carry the energy, resolve, and democratic spirit of this movement into Parliament and intensify the struggle for affordable and quality education for all.CPM general secretary M A Baby said Pradhan's resignation was the first step. "Congratulations to Abhijeet Dipke and CJP, to SFI, AISF, AISA, and lakhs of students and young people for their courage and determination which has won this historic victory. We demand comprehensive reform: scrap NTA! Take back NEP!" CPM said."It is a rare moment of democratic accountability, achieved not through the goodwill of an arrogant govt, but through the sustained struggle of students and youth across the country. The students' movement has defeated the arrogance of BJP and compelled the Modi-Shah regime to answer for its failures," CPI general secretary D Raja said.
Article Summary: Left parties leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which have active units in Delhi. AISA members, despite having no prior association with Abhijeet Dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students.

Article Title: PM Modi is India's past, protesting youth the country's future, says Rahul
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi said "past can never fight the future”.

NEW DELHI: Asserting that "time has come to remove this govt", Congress 's Rahul Gandhi said PM Narendra Modi is India's past while the protesting youth are the country's future. He added that the "past can never fight the future". Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation a "victory of truth and defeat of Modi's stubbornness".Rahul said students' agitation has issued a warning that if BJP-RSS continue to run the govt like their personal fiefdom, they would face a stir 10 times more intense than what is happening now. He accused RSS of hollowing India from inside like termites. He said Pradhan's resignation is a signal to other communities that are being "oppressed" by Modi govt, that fighting the govt is a wise step.Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said, "Force was used against them.But the youth did not bend; govt had to bend." She said she had been wondering for the past 10-12 years, "When will we wake up and realise what is being done to our country?" She said the youth are reclaiming their country.Party MP K C Venugopal said, "A massive salute to millions of students across country who compelled this govt to bow down to their will."Rahul said that Pradhan was a symbol of corruption and destruction of world-class education system, and "it is good that he is gone".
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said PM Narendra Modi is India's past while the protesting youth are the country's future. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge called education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation a "victory of truth and defeat of Modi's stubbornness"

Article Title: Bill proposes 3-month deadline for HCs to dispose of paper leak appeals
Article Text:
Bid to make investigation and judicial process time-bound

What changes in New Bill

NEW DELHI: Aiming to ensure faster disposal of exam paper leak cases, govt has proposed a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts, unlike other cases where no such fixed timeline for deciding appeals exists. This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one.According to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill circulated to Lok Sabha MPs Saturday, individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks would face longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.As per the bill, which would be introduced in Lok Sabha Monday, the minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers conducting public examinations, has been increased to five years.In cases involving organised crime, the minimum imprisonment has been proposed at seven years from the current provision of five years. In all these cases, the maximum jail term would be 10 years.For speedy investigations, the bill proposes govt may constitute a central investigation agency or a special task force (STF). Where an STF has been constituted, it would carry out the investigation. The bill also seeks to insert a new provision mandating that every investigation be completed within two months.The bill provides for day-to-day proceedings and empowers states to establish special fast-track courts in consultation with the chief justice of the respective HC.It mandates that such trial proceedings shall continue until all witnesses in attendance have been examined. These courts would be required to dispose of cases within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet. All pending trials will be shifted to the special court, and these must also be disposed of within three months.It proposes that any appeal against an order of a fast-track court shall be heard by a division bench of HC. It proposes that every appeal be filed within 30 days from the date of the fast-track court's order and not after a maximum of 90 days under any circumstances.
Article Summary: Govt proposes a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts. This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one. Minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers has been increased to five years.

Article Title: Pradhan’s five-year term built operating system for NEP, but exam crisis cast shadow
Article Text:
Dharmendra Pradhan (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Dharmendra Pradhan , who stepped down as Union education minister on Saturday after a five-year tenure, leaves behind an education system more standardised, digitally connected and centrally regulated than the one he inherited — but also questions over examination credibility, institutional autonomy, data privacy and the Centre’s capacity to implement reforms on such a large scale.Pradhan, the longest-serving education minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet, held the portfolio from July 7, 2021, to July 25, 2026. Until 2024, he was also minister for skill development and entrepreneurship.His tenure was less about announcing a new education policy — the National Education Policy had been approved in 2020 — and more about constructing the machinery required to put it into operation.The defining theme was standardisation and portability: common entrance examinations, transferable academic credits, permanent student identification numbers, comparable assessment standards and an attempted umbrella regulator for higher education.The Common University Entrance Test, introduced in 2022, sought to replace differing Class XII board cut-offs with a common admission platform for central universities.It also dramatically expanded the role of the National Testing Agency, whose functioning and credibility later became one of the biggest challenges of Pradhan’s tenure.The National Credit Framework, Academic Bank of Credits and four-year undergraduate programmes were designed to allow students to accumulate and transfer credits, pursue multidisciplinary courses and enter or leave programmes without losing their academic record.APAAR, envisaged as a permanent academic identity for every student, sought to link school, university and skill qualifications through DigiLocker and the credit bank. While intended to ease mobility, it triggered concerns over consent and protection of children’s data.In school education, the ministry released curriculum frameworks for the foundational stage and school education, operationalising the NEP’s 5+3+3+4 structure. PM SHRI was launched to upgrade more than 14,500 existing government schools as models of NEP implementation, while PARAKH was established to develop common assessment standards and bring greater comparability among school boards.Other big-ticket measures included the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, One Nation One Subscription for access to research journals, PM-USHA funding for state universities, permission for foreign universities to open campuses in India and the establishment of IIT campuses abroad.Pradhan also pushed Indian-language textbooks, multidisciplinary education, vocational integration and apprenticeship programmes, drawing on the overlap between his education and skill-development portfolios.The proposed replacement of UGC, AICTE and NCTE with an umbrella regulatory architecture remained unfinished. Implementation also met resistance from some states over language, curriculum and centrally sponsored schemes.Ultimately, the sharpest contradiction of the Pradhan years lay in national testing. Common examinations were meant to deliver fairness and uniformity, but paper leaks, cancellations and administrative failures raised doubts about whether centralisation had moved faster than institutional capacity.
Article Summary: Pradhan was the longest-serving education minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s cabinet. He held the portfolio from July 7, 2021, to July 25, 2026. His tenure was less about announcing a new education policy and more about constructing machinery required to put it into operation.

Article Title: "Unwavering commitment to ethical values": Delhi CM Rekha Gupta praises Dharmendra Pradhan following resignation
Article Text:
"Unwavering commitment to ethical values": Delhi CM Rekha Gupta praises Dharmendra Pradhan following resignation

माननीय श्री @dpradhanbjp जी ने अपने सार्वजनिक जीवन में हर दायित्व को निष्ठा, ईमानदारी और पूर्ण समर्पण के साथ निभाया है। केंद्रीय शिक्षा मंत्री के रूप में उन्होंने राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति-2020 को प्रभावी रूप से लागू करने में महत्वपूर्ण योगदान दिया। शिक्षा व्यवस्था में अनेक सार्थक... https://t.co/6wUoyXfO8h- Rekha Gupta (@gupta_rekha) July 25, 2026

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday lauded Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation from the Cabinet and his tenure and principled stance, describing his decision to step down as a testament to his dedication to public ethics and national interest.In a post on X, Gupta commended Pradhan's contributions to India's educational landscape, particularly highlighting his role in rolling out key policy frameworks and promoting Indian languages in academia."Honorable Shri @dpradhanbjp Ji has fulfilled every responsibility in his public life with dedication, honesty, and complete devotion. As the Union Education Minister, he made a significant contribution to the effective implementation of the National Education Policy-2020.He advanced numerous meaningful reforms in the education system. Education in Indian languages received a boost, technical and higher education expanded, and new opportunities became available for students. "Addressing the minister's decision to step down, Chief Minister Gupta emphasised that prioritizing national interest over position exemplifies high moral standards in governance."Prioritizing the national interest above all, he has submitted his resignation from his position.This decision reflects his unwavering commitment to ethical values, dignity, and principles in public life. May his continuous efforts in the service of the nation continually reach new heights. Heartfelt best wishes for his bright future."Gupta wished Pradhan success in his future endeavours and said, "May his continuous efforts in the service of the nation continually reach new heights. Heartfelt best wishes for his bright future."Pradhan's resignation came after a month-long agitation at Jantar Mantar led by Cockroach Janata Party and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who sat for a 26-day-long hunger strike as the NEET-UG exam was leaked in May. The re-examination was held on June 21.The momentum peaked on July 20 with CJP's 'Chalo Sansad' march, which was met with police action.Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke, in his first reaction, said, "We have done it. Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned.""Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. And this resignation is proof that if you people are not afraid, if you people do not bow down to this government, then we can take the resignation of anyone," he added.
Article Summary: Pradhan's resignation came after a month-long agitation at Jantar Mantar led by Cockroach Janata Party and activist Sonam Wangchuk. Gupta commended Pradhan's contributions to India's educational landscape, particularly highlighting his role in rolling out key policy frameworks.

Article Title: 'This was a warning from students & oppn': Rahul attacks Centre, PM Modi after CJP ends stir
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday hailed Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as the "victory of the future of India."During a press conference, the Congress leader said the country's education system had been under attack for years and that the government would have to take concrete steps to bring about reforms."First of all, this is the victory of our students. This is the future of India. The education system which used to be our pride, the whole world acknowledged that the education system of India is very good. It has been under attack for years. That is the basic message."He also targeted Union home minister Amit Shah over the alleged brutality against protesters marching to Parliament on July 20 and claimed that the issue would be prominently raised by the Opposition during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament."We hold Mr Amit Shah directly responsible for the violence that has taken place against our students. He had sought Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of students who died by suicide following the paper leak and action against police personnel over the alleged crackdown on protesters on July 20.However, following three rounds of talks with the Centre, the CJP on Sunday announced that it was withdrawing its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar with immediate effect after the government accepted its remaining demands, while also agreeing to consider the party's five-point charter on examination reforms.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi hails resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan as "victory of the future of India" Congress leader says the country's education system had been under attack for years. He also targeted Union home minister Amit Shah over the alleged brutality against protesters marching to Parliament.

Article Title: Similar symptoms, climate change & testing gaps: Why monsoon illnesses are so often misdiagnosed
Article Text:
Representational image

Impact on newborns

Why the risk is higher among children

Contribution of climate change

Government data reflects rise in malaria cases during the pre-monsoon months

Why diagnosis gets delayed

Nitish Kumar, 22, a student from Nawada, Bihar, first relied on over-the-counter medicines when he began experiencing symptoms of chikungunya in February last year. For almost a week, he believed it was an ordinary viral fever.“I did not immediately go to a doctor. I bought some medicines from a pharmacy to treat the symptoms of what I thought was a viral fever and made some changes to my diet.”Even after seeing a doctor, the mosquito-borne viral disease went undetected. “One day, I noticed a sudden eruption of red spots on my body, and I suspected I was infected with chikungunya. I went to AIIMS Bhopal to see a doctor, but the doctor handed me a list of medicines prescribed for viral fever.Even the doctor could not diagnose it initially despite the rash.”The World Health Organization (WHO) notes that chikungunya symptoms — abrupt fever, swelling, muscle pain, headache, nausea, fatigue — overlap with those of other infections, making misdiagnosis common. If the illness lacks severe joint pain, it may go unnoticed because symptoms in many infected individuals are mild.This is hardly an outlier. The initial symptoms of most monsoon-related illnesses closely overlap with those of common viral fever.“This is a typical situation observed during the rainy season. We come across many cases of patients who present with symptoms such as fever, sore throat, or general body weakness and are treated as viral infections. But after 2 to 3 days, if the high fever persists, body pains, or low platelets indicate influenza or dengue,” said Dr. M. J. Jayakanth, Consultant — Internal Medicine, SPARSH Hospital, Sarjapur Road, Bangalore.For dengue, WHO says most people are asymptomatic, while symptomatic cases experience high fever, headache, body aches, nausea and rash. Malaria’s mild symptoms are similar: fever, chills and headache.The monsoon brings relief from summer heat, especially in northern India, but also a hidden cost: a surge of infections. Pools of stagnant water left by heavy downpours become mosquito breeding grounds, fueling spread of vector-borne illnesses like malaria, dengue and chikungunya. Heavy rainfall and high humidity also allow airborne viruses, including influenza, to linger longer, and as people retreat indoors, close contact in poorly ventilated spaces facilitates transmission. Because many monsoon illnesses begin with fever and headache — symptoms associated with viral fever — delayed detection can allow them to worsen into life-threatening conditions.Dr Manish Mittal, senior consultant paediatrician at Cocoon Hospital in Jaipur, says newborns and toddlers are more vulnerable during the monsoon because of immature immune systems. “The combination of high humidity, pollution through dirty water, a moist environment, and mosquitoes increases their susceptibility to lung infections, diarrhoea, skin infections, and vector-borne diseases. Even a small infection may develop into something serious in infants. ”Delayed detection is common in children because they cannot always communicate symptoms clearly. “Parents sometimes seek medical care only after dehydration, persistent fever, or unusual lethargy develops, which can delay timely diagnosis and treatment.”Dr. Mittal recommends parents ensure hygiene at home: keep surroundings dry, use clean water, protect babies from mosquitoes, and continue breastfeeding if feasible. “If the infant has fever, poor feeding, lethargy, vomiting, diarrhoea, low urine output, or difficulty breathing, prompt medical care is required.”On the UNDP blog, Kathryn Johnson, a policy specialist in HIV and health for the UNDP regional office for Asia-Pacific, writes that changing rainfall patterns and rising temperatures increase the risk of vector-borne diseases in rapidly urbanising regions with weak health infrastructure. “Warmer climates extend the breeding seasons and geographical range of many vectors, while increased rainfall or poor water management in urban settings provides ideal conditions for their spread. ”This complicates diagnosis, as these diseases are no longer confined to the monsoon season.Abhay Tripathi, 22, a journalism student at Central University of Odisha, says he contracted chikungunya last May in Bhopal, a month of high temperatures. Because it wasn’t monsoon, he assumed it was ordinary fever. “I did not go to the doctor on the first day because, being a student living away from home, I thought it was just a fever. I took a paracetamol that I had in my room and rested for a day. But on the second day, the fever didn't break, and I noticed minor rashes on my hand. I got worried and decided to see a doctor.”Government data show rising malaria cases in pre- and post-monsoon months. The National Centre for Vector-Borne Disease Control’s monthly report records a slight rise in positive malaria cases in 2025 during pre-monsoon months compared with 2024. Mapped against the three-year average, the increase is significant, especially in months approaching peak summer.Dr. Jayakanth says climate change is not the sole contributor. Improved testing and surveillance have picked up cases that earlier went unreported. “Urban water storage, construction sites, poor drainage, and changing human movement patterns also create year-round breeding habitats.”“So, this trend is probably not due to a single factor; it reflects a combination of climate change, environmental changes, urbanisation, and better disease detection systems,” he adds.Gaps remain in diagnostic infrastructure and mechanisms, including low availability of rapid diagnostic tests in peripheral areas, delays in laboratory results, poor early screening, and limited healthcare infrastructure in both urban and rural areas. “Most primary hospitals do not have the infrastructure to conduct tests on-site, meaning that the samples will be taken to external laboratories, hence causing a delay,” he says.Ultimately, this escalating public health challenge is more than a seasonal inconvenience. Climate change is reshaping environmental patterns and vector habitats, while access to advanced diagnostics remains unequal — a convergence that is intensifying the risk and reach of these illnesses.
Article Summary: The monsoon brings relief from summer heat, especially in northern India, but also a hidden cost: a surge of infections. Pools of stagnant water left by heavy downpours become mosquito breeding grounds, fueling spread of vector-borne illnesses. Heavy rainfall and high humidity also allow airborne viruses, including influenza, to linger longer.

Article Title: 'Thank you for your relentless service to nation': BJP leaders react to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Dharmendra Pradhan (File photo)

NEW DELHI: BJP leaders on Saturday paid tribute to Dharmendra Pradhan after he resigned as Union education minister amid nationwide student protests demanding his resignation over the alleged NEET (UG) paper leak and related controversies.BJP national president Nitin Nabin thanked Pradhan for "prioritising larger interests.""As Union Education Minister, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan Ji played a pivotal role in reforming India's education landscape and successfully implementing the landmark National Education Policy (NEP 2020), among other initiatives. I extend my best wishes for his future endeavors," Nabin said on X.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju thanked Pradhan for his "relentless service" to the nation, describing his tenure as a testament to decades of public service and commitment to student welfare."True leadership is measured over decades & @dpradhanbjp ji’s journey stands as a testament to lifelong engagement with public life & student welfare.Having worked alongside him in the Union Cabinet, I have seen his sincere dedication to strengthening India’s education ecosystem & keeping our millions of young students at the center of every decision. I wish you the very best as you continue to serve the nation with the same conviction & sincerity!" he added.Rajya Sabha MP and BJP national general secretary Vinod Tawde said Pradhan had always accorded the "highest importance" to the idea that "the identity of a strong nation is recognised through its education system.""His journey in public life, which began with the student movement, reached a significant milestone as the country's Education Minister. During this period, he made continuous efforts to keep the importance of education at the center of the national discourse. Best wishes for your future public life, with the hope that your 'Nation First' sentiment remains committed to the goal of a developed India by 2047," Tawde wrote on X.Pradhan's resignation came as youth-led protests at Jantar Mantar in Delhi—the capital's designated protest site—intensified, with demonstrators demanding his resignation.
